blocks.text: Condo buildings in Stave Falls

Stave Falls is inside the City of Mission — unlike Dewdney-Deroche (FVRD Electoral Area G) and Lake Errock (FVRD Electoral Area C). The City of Mission's own Rural Mission Strategy page names Stave Falls first among the rural communities it covers — "From Stave Falls, Steelhead and Silverdale to our other rural neighbourhoods" — and ties that work to the City's Official Community Plan. So City of Mission planning, zoning and tax rules are the relevant municipal frame here, and the rural-area (Province) tax regime does not apply.
Streets, schools and transit near Stave Falls condos

items.t: This page covers the Stave Falls community in the northern part of the City of Mission, around Stave Lake, Hayward Lake and the Stave River. Listings here carry the board sub-area "Stave Falls" and a "Mission" mailing address (postal codes V4S 1xx), on streets including Wilson Street, Dewdney Trunk Road, Berg Avenue, Rolley Lake Street, Carr Street and Glacier Drive.

The name: "Stave Falls" is both the community name and the name of the falls/power site on the Stave River — BC Hydro's Powerhouse at Stave Falls, built in 1912, was once B.C.'s biggest hydroelectric power source and is now a BC Hydro Visitor Centre and National Historic Site.

The hydro system, from BC Hydro: a three-reservoir, three-generating-station system — water stored in Alouette Lake runs through Alouette Generating Station into Stave Lake, flows through the new powerhouse at Stave Falls into Hayward Lake, and finally through Ruskin Dam and Powerhouse before spilling into the Fraser River three kilometres south. The reservoirs are popular recreation areas; swimming, hiking, biking, fishing and boating are all options, and Hayward Lake in particular gets busy in summer.

Community park project: the City of Mission's engagement site covers a Stave Falls Community Park on Brackley Avenue, designed through a May 2023 community session beside the school, with entryways and park access from Brackley Avenue and the school.

items.t: The FVRD/Province frame used for Dewdney-Deroche and Lake Errock does not apply here.

Mission property taxes: Stave Falls properties are inside the City of Mission and pay municipal taxes to the City. City of Mission 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a flat 10% penalty on balances unpaid after July 2 — the City's tax page states: "A 10% penalty will be added to any current balances outstanding (including unclaimed home owner grants) on July 3, 2026." The flat 10% is the penalty under the Community Charter general tax collection scheme (ss. 233–234) as set by the Municipal Tax Regulation, B.C. Reg. 426/2003, s. 3; Mission has no alternative-scheme bylaw, and the rural-area penalty rules (5% + 5% to October 31, paid to the Province) do not apply inside the City.

The name and the hydro system: "Stave Falls" is both the community name and the name of the falls/power site on the Stave River. BC Hydro's Powerhouse at Stave Falls was built in 1912, was once B.C.'s biggest hydroelectric power source, and remained in operation until a new powerhouse was built in 2000; the old powerhouse is now a BC Hydro Visitor Centre and National Historic Site. BC Hydro describes a three-reservoir, three-generating-station system — water stored in Alouette Lake runs through Alouette Generating Station into Stave Lake, flows through the new powerhouse at Stave Falls into Hayward Lake, and finally through Ruskin Dam and Powerhouse before spilling into the Fraser River.

Recreation: BC Hydro's Hayward Lake recreation area, near Mission on the Stave River system, is the area's anchor recreation site — the reservoir is an active hydroelectric facility and a popular recreation area, and the nearby Stave Lake boat launch and Ruskin Dam recreation area are also BC Hydro sites; the City of Mission restricts parking on city roads leading to Hayward Lake at busy times.
Nearby areas: Steelhead to the west/southwest, Mission West and Silverdale to the south, Ruskin and Hayward Lake across the Stave River side, and Durieu / the Hatzic Valley to the east.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Stave Falls

items.t: City plans and zoning (local): Mission's Lougheed Highway Corridor Plan is in preparation, not adopted — Council endorsed Focused Land Use Option #2 on July 20, 2026. A specific lot's OCP designation and zone: confirm with the City before quoting density or second-dwelling potential. The FVRD/Province frame used for Dewdney-Deroche and Durieu does not apply here.

Secondary suites and SSMUH: a Mission secondary suite is a self-contained living space inside a single family home forming part of the same real estate entity; a suite is not a coach home or garden cottage (those are detached secondary dwellings); suites are not permitted in townhouses or rowhomes; all suites must be registered with the City, new suites go through the building permit process, and an annual secondary suite fee of $63 plus utility fees applies. Mission has adopted the provincial SSMUH legislation — zones previously restricted to single-family or duplex dwellings as of December 7, 2023 are subject to it, subject to eligibility and servicing; Stave Falls' rural lots sit outside the urban serviced area.

Wells and septic: wells are recorded in the provincial GWELLS database, and onsite sewerage must comply with the Sewerage System Regulation, including the 30 m setback from a well unless professional advice is obtained.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Stave Falls

items.t: SSMUH and suites: the City has adopted the provincial SSMUH legislation for zones previously restricted to single-family or duplex dwellings, subject to eligibility and servicing. Mission suites must be registered with the City and are not permitted in townhouses or rowhomes — there are no townhouses here for that rule to apply to. Listing text from a Nov 2, 2026 search for Stave Falls-area land describes RR7S zoning allowing two dwelling units (suites or carriage homes) on specific Carr Street lots; that is listing text for those lots only, not a zone rule for the sub-area.

City property taxes — flat 10% (City ground, because Stave Falls is inside the City): City of Mission 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a flat 10% penalty on balances unpaid after July 2 — the City's tax page states: "A 10% penalty will be added to any current balances outstanding (including unclaimed home owner grants) on July 3, 2026" (Community Charter ss. 233–234 + Municipal Tax Regulation, B.C. Reg. 426/2003, s. 3; Mission has no s. 235 alternative-scheme bylaw). The rural regime does not apply here: 5% after July 2 + a further 5% after October 31 (Taxation (Rural Area) Act s. 11) is for FVRD electoral areas outside the City — state both regimes only to keep them apart, and quote the flat 10% for a Stave Falls parcel inside the City.

Manufactured-home pad rent (MHPTA), where a park home is the purchase instead: pad-rent increases are capped at 2.3% plus a proportional amount for 2026, and 2.2% plus a proportional amount for 2027 — confirmed from the park's own tenancy documents for any specific pad.
Waterfront reality: the Stave/Hayward shoreline is a working BC Hydro reservoir system (Alouette Lake → Stave Lake → Stave Falls powerhouse → Hayward Lake → Ruskin Dam → Fraser River).

Taxes and rebates (worked example, inputs stated): PTT is 1% on the first $200,000, 2% from $200,000 to $2 million, 3% above $2 million, plus a further 2% on the residential portion above $3 million; a page row "Over $3M — 5%" is a compression of 3% + 2% — the tier math governs. On a $900,000 fee-simple acreage house with no exemption: 1% × $200,000 ($2,000) + 2% × $700,000 ($14,000) = $16,000. First-time buyers — exempt on the first $500,000 at $835,000 or less, partial to $860,000; newly built home exemption — full to $1,100,000, eliminated at $1,150,000. New Housing Rebate 36% / maximum $6,300 / $350K–$450K; HBP $60,000; FHSA $40,000 lifetime / $8,000 per year; CMHC premiums 0.6%–4.5%. Manufactured homes on rented pads commonly face different lender treatment than fee-simple homes — confirm financing for the specific tenure before writing.
Foreclosure note: Mission has no Supreme Court registry.

items.t: Stave Falls is a city address with a rural market — and the two must not be priced or taxed as each other. Inside the City for OCP, zoning and the flat 10% penalty; acreage, wells, septic and reservoir shoreline for the actual purchase. The neighbouring areas (Dewdney-Deroche, Lake Errock) sit in FVRD electoral areas under the rural tax regime — the boundary between those regimes is a municipal line, not a feel.

The "lake" is a power system. Water stored in Alouette Lake runs through Alouette Generating Station into Stave Lake, through the new Stave Falls powerhouse into Hayward Lake, and through Ruskin Dam into the Fraser River three kilometres south — shoreline use sits inside a working hydro system, which is why dock and moorage claims need BC Hydro and title answers, not listing text.

The old powerhouse outlived its job by a century's turn. Built in 1912, once B.C.'s biggest hydroelectric power source, operating until a new powerhouse replaced it in 2000 — now a Visitor Centre, museum and National Historic Site.

The page's 28 results include land and manufactured homes the board's September 2026 residential splits do not count the same way. Quoting either number as the other is the standing error for this page.
A fresh townhouse search for this area returns other places' stock. A buyer who stops at the search result will think Stave Falls has strata product; on the record, it does not.

The community park exists as a design, not yet as a confirmed opening. The City's engagement page covers design concepts for a park on Brackley Avenue beside the school, with a survey that closed May 11, 2025.

Hayward Lake is the busy shore, not Stave Lake. Per BC Hydro, the reservoirs offer swimming, hiking, biking, fishing and boating, and Hayward Lake in particular gets busy in summer with swimmers and paddlers — the recreation pitch and the property's actual shoreline are two different checks.

ALR, wells, septic and the hydro shoreline: ALR status is per-parcel — check the ALC's ALR Property and Map Finder; on ALR parcels the ALC frame is one principal residence at a maximum of 500 m² plus at most one additional residence of 90 m² (≤40 ha) or 186 m² (>40 ha), and depositing a strata plan causes subdivision in the ALR and needs ALC permission (ALC Information Bulletin 09, s.6). Wells are recorded in the provincial gwells database, and onsite sewerage must comply with the Sewerage System Regulation, including the 30 m setback from a well unless professional advice is obtained.

blocks.text: Jared's take on Stave Falls

Around Stave Lake, Hayward Lake and the Stave River, Stave Falls is Mission’s waterfront community, a rural area inside city limits. One thing buyers need to know: the shoreline is a BC Hydro reservoir.

faq.a: The stock is acreage houses, vacant acreage lots and manufactured homes in Wilson Street parks. A buyer who wants a Mission condo is buying in central Mission, documented in that area's condo notes — not in Stave Falls.
faq.q: Are there any condos in Stave Falls?

faq.a: The City of Mission. Mission 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a flat 10% penalty added to balances outstanding on July 3, 2026 (Community Charter ss. 233–234 scheme). The rural regime — pay the Province, 5% after July 2 and 5% after October 31 — does not apply inside the City, even though Stave Falls looks and feels rural.
faq.q: What taxes do I pay on a Stave Falls property — City or Province?

faq.a: The community sits in the Stave Lake / Hayward Lake reservoir system — BC Hydro describes water flowing from Stave Lake through the Stave Falls powerhouse into Hayward Lake, with swimming, boating and fishing on the reservoirs.
